topic: After 40, phone at arm's length? Presbyopia explained

youtube.title: After 40, phone at arm's length? 📱 Presbyopia explained #Shorts
youtube.description:
Turned 40 and now you hold your phone at arm's length to read? That's presbyopia.
40 வயதுக்கு மேல் அருகில் படிக்க சிரமமா? இது சாதாரணமான வயது மாற்றம்.

• The lens inside your eye slowly gets stiffer after about 40, so near focus gets harder
• It happens to almost everyone, even people who never wore glasses
• Signs: holding things far, tired eyes after reading, needing brighter light
• Readymade readers use the same power for both eyes; your two eyes may need different powers
• Progressive lenses give far, middle and near vision in one pair
• Sudden change in vision? See an eye specialist the same day

gmb.text: After about 40, many people start holding their phone or newspaper further away to read. This is presbyopia: the natural lens inside the eye slowly becomes stiffer, so focusing up close gets harder. It happens to almost everyone and is not a disease. Common signs are holding things at arm's length, tired eyes or headaches after reading, and needing brighter light. Readymade reading glasses use one power for both eyes, but each eye can need a different power. A full eye test tells you exactly what you need, and progressive lenses can give clear far and near vision in one pair. If your vision changes suddenly, see an eye specialist the same day.
